theory.intro: The equations $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$ describe the path through the parameter $t$. Making $t$ the subject of the first and substituting it into the second links $x$ and $y$ directly.
facts: Eliminating $t$ gives the **Cartesian equation** $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}\cos^{2}\alpha}$, which contains no $t$ and requires non-zero horizontal velocity, $V\cos\alpha\ne 0$.
Since $\sec^{2}\alpha=1+\tan^{2}\alpha$, the same path is also written $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\left(1+\tan^{2}\alpha\right)$.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ is negative, so the path is a parabola opening downwards.
The path only describes the flight. For rightward flight from the origin, its domain is $0\le x\le R$, where $R$ is the range.
When landing is at launch level, setting $y=0$ and taking the non-zero root gives the range $R$. For a platform of height $h$ with the launch point as the origin, use the ground level $y=-h$ instead.
The gradient $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ gives the direction of motion at a point, through $\tan\phi=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.
At $x=0$ the gradient equals $\tan\alpha$, so it gives the angle of projection.
steps: Make $t$ the subject of the horizontal equation

workedExamples.question_text:
A projectile launched from the origin has $x=30t$ and $y=20t-5t^{2}$, with distances in metres and time in seconds.
(a) Find its Cartesian equation.
(b) Find its range and greatest height.
(c) Find its angle of projection and direction of motion at $x=90$, to 1 d.p.

A projectile follows $y=\dfrac{3}{2}x-\dfrac{x^{2}}{80}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres.
(a) Find its height when $x=20$.
(b) Find both horizontal distances at which its height is $40\text{ m}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Substitute the horizontal distance.
$\begin{aligned}y(20)&=\dfrac{3}{2}(20)-\dfrac{20^{2}}{80}\\&=30-5\\&=25\text{ m}.\end{aligned}$
(b) Set the height equal to $40$.
$\begin{aligned}40&=\dfrac{3}{2}x-\dfrac{x^{2}}{80}\\3200&=120x-x^{2}\\x^{2}-120x+3200&=0\\(x-40)(x-80)&=0.\end{aligned}$
The horizontal distances are $40\text{ m}$ while rising and $80\text{ m}$ while falling.

workedExamples.question_text:
A projectile leaves level ground with $x=Vt\cos\theta$ and $y=Vt\sin\theta-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$, where $V>0$, $g>0$ and $0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$.
(a) Eliminate $t$ to derive its Cartesian equation.
(b) Use this equation to derive the range formula.
(c) Find both projection angles, to 1 d.p., if $V=20\text{ m/s}$, $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the range is $30\text{ m}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) From the horizontal equation, $t=\dfrac{x}{V\cos\theta}$.
$\begin{aligned}y&=V\sin\theta\left(\dfrac{x}{V\cos\theta}\right)-\dfrac{g}{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{V\cos\theta}\right)^{2}\\&=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta.\end{aligned}$
(b) At landing, $y=0$ and $x=R>0$.
$\begin{aligned}R\tan\theta&=\dfrac{gR^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta\\R&=\dfrac{2V^{2}\tan\theta}{g\sec^{2}\theta}\\&=\dfrac{2V^{2}\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}\\&=\dfrac{V^{2}\sin2\theta}{g}.\end{aligned}$
(c) Substitute the speed, gravity and range.
$\begin{aligned}30&=\dfrac{400\sin2\theta}{10}\\\sin2\theta&=\dfrac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}$
Since $0^{\circ}<2\theta<180^{\circ}$, $2\theta\approx48.5904^{\circ}$ or $131.4096^{\circ}$.
The projection angles are $\theta\approx24.3^{\circ}$ or $65.7^{\circ}$.

(a) Integrating the acceleration and applying the initial velocity gives $\dot{x}=10$ and $\dot{y}=10-10t$. Since $x(0)=y(0)=0$, $x=10t$ and $y=10t-5t^{2}$.
From $x=10t$, $t=\dfrac{x}{10}$.
$\begin{aligned}y&=10\left(\dfrac{x}{10}\right)-5\left(\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{2}\\&=x-\dfrac{x^{2}}{20}.\end{aligned}$
(b) Ground level is $y=-15$.
$\begin{aligned}-15&=x-\dfrac{x^{2}}{20}\\x^{2}-20x-300&=0\\(x-30)(x+10)&=0.\end{aligned}$
Rightward flight requires $x\ge0$, so the ball lands $30\text{ m}$ from the base.
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=1-\dfrac{x}{10}\\\left.\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=30}&=-2.\end{aligned}$
Its impact direction is $\tan^{-1}(2)\approx63.4^{\circ}$ below the horizontal.

workedExamples.question_text:
A projectile launched from level ground follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$, with $0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$.
(a) Use differentiation to show that its greatest height is $\dfrac{V^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$.
(b) Find $\theta$ if $V=30\text{ m/s}$, $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the greatest height is $\dfrac{45}{4}\text{ m}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) At the vertex, the gradient is zero.
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx\sec^{2}\theta}{V^{2}}\\0&=\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx\sec^{2}\theta}{V^{2}}\\x&=\dfrac{V^{2}\tan\theta}{g\sec^{2}\theta}\\&=\dfrac{V^{2}\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}.\end{aligned}$
Substitute this horizontal coordinate into the path equation.
$\begin{aligned}H&=\dfrac{V^{2}\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}\tan\theta-\dfrac{g\sec^{2}\theta}{2V^{2}}\left(\dfrac{V^{2}\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}\right)^{2}\\&=\dfrac{V^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{g}-\dfrac{V^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}\\&=\dfrac{V^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}.\end{aligned}$
The quadratic coefficient is negative, so this vertex gives the greatest height.
(b)
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{45}{4}&=\dfrac{900\sin^{2}\theta}{20}\\\sin^{2}\theta&=\dfrac{1}{4}\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{1}{2}\\\theta&=30^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A projectile leaves the origin at $30\text{ m/s}$ and angle $\theta$, where $0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Its path is $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{5x^{2}}{900}\sec^{2}\theta$.
It passes through $(45,\dfrac{45}{4})$. Find both possible projection angles, to 1 d.p.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Substitute the point and use $\sec^{2}\theta=1+\tan^{2}\theta$.
$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{45}{4}&=45\tan\theta-\dfrac{45}{4}\sec^{2}\theta\\1&=4\tan\theta-\left(1+\tan^{2}\theta\right)\\\tan^{2}\theta-4\tan\theta+2&=0\\\tan\theta&=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{16-8}}{2}\\&=2\pm\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}$
Both values are positive. The projection angles are $\theta=\tan^{-1}(2-\sqrt{2})\approx30.4^{\circ}$ or $\theta=\tan^{-1}(2+\sqrt{2})\approx73.7^{\circ}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A shell leaves the origin with speed $V$ and elevation $\alpha$, where $0^{\circ}<\alpha<90^{\circ}$, following $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$.
(a) Express this as a quadratic in $\tan\alpha$.
(b) Find both elevations, to the nearest minute, that reach a target $1500\text{ m}$ horizontally and $250\text{ m}$ vertically from the gun when $V=100\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$ and $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Use $\sec^{2}\alpha=1+\tan^{2}\alpha$, multiply by $2V^{2}$ and collect terms.
$\begin{aligned}2V^{2}y&=2xV^{2}\tan\alpha-gx^{2}\left(1+\tan^{2}\alpha\right)\\gx^{2}\tan^{2}\alpha-2xV^{2}\tan\alpha+2yV^{2}+gx^{2}&=0.\end{aligned}$
(b) Convert all distances to metres and use $V^{2}=20000$.
$\begin{aligned}22500000\tan^{2}\alpha-60000000\tan\alpha+32500000&=0\\9\tan^{2}\alpha-24\tan\alpha+13&=0\\\tan\alpha&=\dfrac{24\pm\sqrt{576-468}}{18}\\&=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}$
Taking inverse tangents without intermediate rounding gives $\alpha\approx37^{\circ}5'$ or $62^{\circ}22'$.

foundation.question_text:
A projectile launched from the origin has $x=20t$ and $y=25t-5t^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres.
Find the Cartesian equation of its path.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Make $t$ the subject of the horizontal equation**
$t=\dfrac{x}{20}$
2. **Substitute into the vertical equation**
$y=25\left(\dfrac{x}{20}\right)-5\left(\dfrac{x}{20}\right)^{2}$
3. **Simplify to a quadratic in $x$**
$=\dfrac{5x}{4}-\dfrac{5x^{2}}{400}$
$=\dfrac{5x}{4}-\dfrac{x^{2}}{80}$

development.question_text:
A projectile is launched from the origin with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, so that $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$.
Show that $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$.
development.solution_text:
1. **Make $t$ the subject of the horizontal equation**
$t=\dfrac{x}{V\cos\alpha}$
2. **Substitute into the vertical equation**
$y=V\sin\alpha\left(\dfrac{x}{V\cos\alpha}\right)-\dfrac{1}{2}g\left(\dfrac{x}{V\cos\alpha}\right)^{2}$
3. **Simplify to a quadratic in $x$**
$=\dfrac{x\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}\cos^{2}\alpha}$
$=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$

development.question_text:
An object is rolled horizontally off the top of a $20\text{ m}$ tower with initial velocity $5\underset{\sim}{i}$ metres per second.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the point of projection as the origin.
Find the Cartesian equation of the path, and how far from the base of the tower the object lands.
development.solution_text:
$\dot{x}=5$ and $\dot{y}=-10t$
$x=5t$ and $y=-5t^{2}$
$t=\dfrac{x}{5}$
$y=-5\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{2}$
$=-\dfrac{x^{2}}{5}$
The ground is at $y=-20$.
$-20=-\dfrac{x^{2}}{5}$
$x^{2}=100$
$x=10$
The object lands $10\text{ m}$ from the base of the tower.

development.question_text:
A projectile launched from the origin at speed $V$ and angle $\theta$ follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$.
Show that the range is $\dfrac{V^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g}$, and hence find the two possible values of $\theta$, to 1 d.p., when $V=30\text{ m/s}$, $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the range is $75\text{ m}$.

A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{5}{324}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres.
Find the two horizontal distances at which its height is $19\text{ m}$, to 1 d.p.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{5}{324}x^{2}=19$
Multiplying by $324$:
$432x-5x^{2}=6156$
$5x^{2}-432x+6156=0$
$x=\dfrac{432\pm\sqrt{186624-123120}}{10}$
$=\dfrac{432\pm 252}{10}$
$x=18$ or $x=68.4$
The height is $19\text{ m}$ at $18\text{ m}$ on the way up and at $68.4\text{ m}$ on the way down.

development.question_text:
A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=2x-\dfrac{1}{50}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres.
Find the range and the greatest height.
development.solution_text:
$2x-\dfrac{1}{50}x^{2}=0$
$x\left(2-\dfrac{x}{50}\right)=0$
$x=0$ or $x=100$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2-\dfrac{x}{25}$
$2-\dfrac{x}{25}=0$
$x=50$
$y(50)=2(50)-\dfrac{1}{50}(50)^{2}$
$=100-50$
$=50$
The range is $100\text{ m}$ and the greatest height is $50\text{ m}$.

development.question_text:
A ball is tossed from a point $O$ that is $6\text{ m}$ above the ground, at $24\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and $O$ as the origin.
Show that the path is $y=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x-\dfrac{5}{432}x^{2}$, and find the horizontal distance travelled when the ball strikes the ground, to 1 d.p.
development.solution_text:
$\dot{x}=24\cos 30^{\circ}=12\sqrt{3}$ and $\dot{y}=-10t+12$
$x=12\sqrt{3}t$ and $y=-5t^{2}+12t$
$t=\dfrac{x}{12\sqrt{3}}$
$y=12\left(\dfrac{x}{12\sqrt{3}}\right)-5\left(\dfrac{x}{12\sqrt{3}}\right)^{2}$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x-\dfrac{5}{432}x^{2}$
The ground is at $y=-6$, so with $x=D$:
$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}D-\dfrac{5}{432}D^{2}=-6$
$5D^{2}-144\sqrt{3}D-2592=0$
$D=\dfrac{144\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{62208+51840}}{10}$
$\approx 58.7$
The ball lands $58.7\text{ m}$ horizontally from $O$.

mastery.question_text:
A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$.
It is launched at $V=20\text{ m/s}$ with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and passes through the point $(20,10)$.
Show that $\tan^{2}\theta-4\tan\theta+3=0$, and hence find the two possible angles of projection, to 1 d.p.

A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$.
Show that its greatest height is $\dfrac{V^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$, and hence find $\theta$ when $V=20\text{ m/s}$, $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the greatest height is $15\text{ m}$.

A shell is fired from a gun at the origin with speed $V=200\text{ m/s}$ and elevation $\alpha$, taking $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the path $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$.
Show that $gx^{2}\tan^{2}\alpha-2xV^{2}\tan\alpha+\left(2yV^{2}+gx^{2}\right)=0$, and hence find the two elevations that hit a target $3\text{ km}$ away horizontally and $0.5\text{ km}$ above the gun, to the nearest minute.
mastery.solution_text:
$y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\left(1+\tan^{2}\alpha\right)$
Multiplying by $2V^{2}$ and collecting terms:
$gx^{2}\tan^{2}\alpha-2xV^{2}\tan\alpha+\left(2yV^{2}+gx^{2}\right)=0$
With $x=3000$, $y=500$, $V=200$ and $g=10$:
$9\times 10^{7}\tan^{2}\alpha-2.4\times 10^{8}\tan\alpha+1.3\times 10^{8}=0$
$9\tan^{2}\alpha-24\tan\alpha+13=0$
$\tan\alpha=\dfrac{24\pm\sqrt{576-468}}{18}$
$=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{3}}{3}$
$\alpha\approx 62^{\circ}22'$ or $\alpha\approx 37^{\circ}5'$
